highest_reported.source: OEIS A250000, Kamenetsky's n=30 layout, with the sequence entry attributing the n<=30 constructions to Stephen Ainley (1977).
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The supplied 30x30 layout is independently parsed and checked: 131 queens per color and no cross-color attacking pair. This is a lower bound, not a proof of optimality for n=30.

best_human.source: Stephen Ainley, Mathematical Puzzles (1977), as attributed in OEIS A250000; the n=30 layout is preserved by Dmitry Kamenetsky's 2019 file.
best_human.provenance: Traditional human mathematical construction predating modern generative AI. The local witness is a later transcription of the published layout, not a claim to possess Ainley's original working notes.
best_human.evidence_state: Exact 30x30 layout saved and independently verified with 131 queens of each color and zero cross-color attacks.

best_public.source: OEIS A250000, Kamenetsky, Best known solutions for 12<=n<=30, entry a(30)>=131.
best_public.provenance: The public witness is a 2019 text layout. OEIS attributes the n<=30 construction family to Ainley (1977). No AI contribution is indicated for this historical construction.
best_public.evidence_state: The n=30 lower-bound witness is reproduced exactly. No n=30 optimality proof was found in the checked sources.

best_reproduced.verification_method: Validate coordinate types and bounds; recount each army; inspect every white-black pair for row, column, and diagonal attacks.
best_reproduced.origin_type: published historical construction, parsed from the public Kamenetsky layout

frozen_human_baseline.endpoint_policy: The exact integer army size is frozen as H for compatibility score J/H.
frozen_human_baseline.evidence_state: The 2019 board transcription and the locally parsed chart agree and pass the exact checker.

compatibility_score.note: H is the reproduced traditional human construction for n=30. A score above 1 exceeds this witness only; it does not prove optimality.

optimality_status.evidence: The 131 layout is reported as a lower bound. The 2025 Clinch-Drescher-Huynh-Saffidine paper gives an asymptotic upper bound only for sufficiently large n and does not certify n=30. The separate INFORMS study proves n=16 has value 37; that does not resolve n=30.
optimality_status.limitations: The row/column packing bound 225 leaves a finite gap 131..225. The asymptotic bound is not applied to n=30 without a stated threshold.

research_paper.title: Constructions, bounds, and algorithms for peaceable queens
research_paper.relevant_result: The paper presents a local search that quickly finds the Ainley construction and gives an upper bound for all sufficiently large n; it does not assert a proof of optimality at n=30.

exact_small_instance.title: Puzzle—Queen Puzzles: An Educational Approach to Integer Programming Techniques
exact_small_instance.relevant_result: The paper reports a confirmed optimum of 37 for n=16. Earlier OEIS statements that only n<=15 are known are stale; this does not settle n=30.

independent_quantity.method: disjoint occupied line labels in each of four queen directions; independent of pairwise attacks
